title: Influence Under Coordinate Polarization
statement: Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\{-1,1\\}$, and let $(i_1,\\ldots,i_k)$ be any finite list of coordinates in $\\{0,\\ldots,n-1\\}$. Obtain $f^{(i_1,\\ldots,i_k)}$ by successively polarizing in those coordinates: at coordinate $i$, the new value at $x$ is the larger of the two values obtained by setting $x_i$ to $+1$ or $-1$ when $x_i=+1$, and the smaller when $x_i=-1$. For every coordinate set $J\\subseteq\\{0,\\ldots,n-1\\}$ and target sign $b$, the coalitional influence of $f^{(i_1,\\ldots,i_k)}$ toward $b$ is at most that of $f$ toward $b$.
hypotheses_covered: $f$ maps the sign cube to the signs
the coordinate list is finite and each listed coordinate lies in $\\{0,\\ldots,n-1\\}$
